<|det|>table [84, 56, 913, 146]<|/det|>
M-5smoothenTokenRebase Function doesn't Account for the badDebtToInternalize variable
SeverityMediumStatusAcknowledged
<|det|>title [81, 166, 185, 180]<|/det|>Description <|det|>text [80, 183, 725, 198]<|/det|>There is a call to oracleReportSanityChecker.smootherTokenRebase in the <|det|>text [80, 200, 915, 249]<|/det|>_simulateOracleReport function of the Accounting contract. This function smoothens the token rebase while limiting how much ether may be used to update the totalPooledEther variable, which is used in the setTH share rate calculation. <|det|>text [80, 252, 892, 302]<|/det|>This function doesn't account for the _pre.badDebtToInternalize variable, which in a very rare scenario can cause the smoothing logic to pull fewer update.eLRewards than available, so as not to increase the exchange price of the share too much in the oracle update. <|det|>text [80, 305, 880, 337]<|/det|>However, the _pre.badDebtToInternalize will decrease the share price, and if not all the execution layer rewards are pulled from the vault, it can cause a negative rebase. <|det|>text [80, 339, 895, 388]<|/det|>The issue is classified as Medium severity because it may result in a very rare case of a negative rebase that could be resolved by pulling more of the execution layer rewards that are available in the vault. <|det|>title [81, 409, 212, 421]<|/det|>Recommendation <|det|>text [80, 425, 895, 493]<|/det|>We recommend also smoothing the badDebtToInternalize variable in the smoothenTokenRebase function of the OracleReportSanityChecker contract, as missing that variable in the smoothing logic may lead to pulling less ether from the execution layer rewards vault than is possible, which may lead to a negative rebase of stETH. <|det|>title [81, 514, 234, 527]<|/det|>Client's Commentary: <|det|>text [81, 530, 460, 544]<|/det|>Client: https://github.com/lidofinance/core/issues/1375 <|det|>text [80, 548, 738, 562]<|/det|>Actually, we have a question about this. While it's true that _pre.badDebtToInternalize can increase <|det|>text [80, 565, 880, 596]<|/det|>update.postInternalShares, as it is used as a denominator, it will only decrease the share rate, so it won't lead to a larger token rebase. Or did we misunderstand the issue somehow? <|det|>text [80, 600, 911, 649]<|/det|>MixBytes: We analyzed a highly unlikely yet theoretically possible scenario where e1Rewards collection would be insufficient due to OracleSanityChecker constraints, leading to inadequate coverage of the total bad debt (despite potential sufficiency if all rewards were collected), thus forcing a negative rebase that could have been prevented. <|det|>text [80, 669, 714, 683]<|/det|>Client: Looks like it's better to divide this issue in two, because of different origin and structure: <|det|>text [80, 686, 845, 700]<|/det|>badDebtToInternalize-related is definitely correct and can be fixed, while accounting sharesToMintAsFees is more <|det|>text [80, 703, 890, 734]<|/det|>complicated(because it's value depends on the smoothing result) and better be done by switching the semantical context from limiting the rebase to limiting the gross APR(before fee deduction) <|det|>text [80, 738, 788, 752]<|/det|>MixBytes: The issue description related to the sharesToMintAsFees was moved to the Low #13 finding. <|det|>text [80, 755, 911, 787]<|/det|>Client: Supporting increased internal shares would require rewriting the limit logic and complicating the code, but the feature is unlikely to be used. The smoothing mechanism (0.075%/day = 27% APR) almost never triggers, and bad debt <|det|>text [80, 790, 901, 822]<|/det|>internalization is a manual, DAO-governed process that should never occur under normal conditions. Adding complexity for this edge case provides negligible benefit. <|det|>footer [82, 949, 248, 972]<|/det|>MixBytes() <|det|>page_number [880, 951, 916, 970]<|/det|>20
